records.name: East Mt. Airy Neighbors
records.summary: A neighborhood group the City of Philadelphia has registered to be consulted on zoning and development in the Upper Northwest part of the city, East Mt. Airy Neighbors gives neighbors a place to hear about projects and respond.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over. Volunteers can also serve as ambassadors who represent the group at city board meetings and public hearings, such as the Zoning Board of Adjustment and City Council.

schedule.text: Office hours on Tuesday and Thursday, 10 am to 2 pm. The Community Impact Committee meets on the third Monday of the month, 7 to 8 pm, on Zoom.

first_step.how: Register through the Zoom link on the Community Impact Committee page, then attend its third Monday meeting from 7 to 8 pm.
first_step.basis: Meetings are on Zoom with a registration link, and the site invites neighbors to join through an online membership application. The site does not say outright that the committee is open to all.
first_step.what_to_expect: The office is open Tuesday and Thursday from 10 am to 2 pm, and other visits are by appointment. The meetings listed on the site are on Zoom, and one project meeting asked people to register in advance. The site does not state a cost or how long a meeting runs.
first_visit_tips: Register first: the Zoom link goes to a registration page.
Office hours are Tuesday and Thursday, 10 am to 2 pm; other days need an appointment.
Membership is an online application that the site links from its join page.

records.notes: The site lists office hours but no office street address and no cost. The group's own site gives info@eastmtairyneighbors.org as its general email; the City list and the RCO page use RCO@, so the carried address is kept. The events page lists flyers only, with a first-Monday chair yoga class and a Thursday board game session at Lonnie Young Recreation Center; it does not say who runs them, so they are not written as group programs. The committee page also carries City Council budget and agenda items dated March 2026 that look copied from the City, so they were not counted as group activity. Status is kept at active on the June 2, 2026 RCO meeting notice.

records.name: Fernhill Food Forest
records.summary: A community-led food forest in Fernhill Park in Southwest Germantown. Neighbors plant and tend fruit trees, berry bushes, herbs, and vegetables on public land, and neighbors are invited to eat what grows.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer during the Saturday open hours. Volunteers water new trees, weed, spread mulch, and help with planting and community work days. Weavers Way Co-op members can earn co-op volunteer hours here, and local schools have held student work days.

schedule.text: Open volunteer hours every Saturday, 10 am to 12 pm.

first_step.how: Come to a Saturday open volunteer hour, 10 am to 12 pm, in Fernhill Park.
first_step.basis: The group's article says anyone can help during the Saturday open hours. The page does not say whether advance sign-up is needed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Saturday hours run from 10 am to noon, and the group says anyone can help. Tasks include watering newly planted trees, weeding, spreading mulch, and planting or community work days when they are scheduled. The site does not state a cost, and Weavers Way co-op members can count their hours here.
first_visit_tips: Email fernhillfoodforest@gmail.com to confirm the meeting spot before you come, since the article gives no street address.
Plan on outdoor, hands-on work such as weeding and mulching.
Weavers Way Co-op members can count these hours toward their co-op volunteer time.

records.notes: Website problem: friendsoffernhill.com, with and without www, returns a 301 redirect to coloksgp36.com, which does not look like this group. The redirect was not followed. The website field is kept as carried, but verify it before this record goes live. Status changed from active to probably_active: the newest dated item I could read is the Resolve Philly article (published September 30, 2024, updated November 14, 2024). The City garden list's 2026 date is a registry entry, not activity. The article gives no street address or cost; the street address above comes from the City garden record in the batch. Partners named in the article are in leads_only.

records.name: Germantown United CDC
records.summary: Germantown United CDC is a Neighborhood Advisory Committee listed by the City of Philadelphia, a local community organization that works with the City on services and priorities in the Upper Northwest part of the city.
records.what_you_do: Work with neighbors and the City on local services and what the area needs.

first_step.how: Call or email the contact on the City list to ask how neighbors take part in meetings and programs.
first_step.basis: The group's website showed no readable text on three attempts, so the only way in is an office phone and email from the City list.

records.notes: The website (germantownunitedcdc.org, tried three times including with www) returned no readable text, so there are no program, meeting, membership or volunteer details from the group itself. Status changed from active to unknown because the only evidence is the City's Neighborhood Advisory Committee list. Owner may want to confirm by phone before publishing. The City list calls the group a Neighborhood Advisory Committee while the name says CDC; the summary is kept as carried.

records.name: Mighty Writers
records.summary: A free nonprofit that helps Philadelphia kids get better at writing. Volunteers help with homework at its after-school Academy, mentor one young writer over time, or help with food and diaper distribution.
records.what_you_do: Writing Assistants help students with homework and writing, one shift of 1 to 4 hours a week, at select locations. Mentors meet their mentee 2 to 4 times a month for at least a year, and Big Brothers Big Sisters handles screening and matching. Distribution volunteers work one 3 to 4 hour shift a week, unloading deliveries and running food and diaper distribution.

schedule.text: After-School Academy runs Monday to Friday, 3 to 6 pm. Writing Assistants work one 1 to 4 hour shift a week, and mentors meet 2 to 4 times a month.

cost.text: All of the group's programs are free.

first_step.how: Submit the volunteer registration form from the group's volunteer page, then email volunteers@mightywriters.org with any questions about clearances.
first_step.basis: Volunteering starts with a registration form, role-based clearances and an orientation, and the site does not say what happens after you apply.
first_step.what_to_expect: Writing Assistants give one 1 to 4 hour shift a week at the after-school Academy, helping with homework and writing and sometimes at snack time or outdoor play. Volunteers commit to at least six months, and staff walk new volunteers through clearances during orientation. Mentors meet a student 2 to 4 times a month for at least a year, and Big Brothers Big Sisters handles their screening and training.
first_visit_tips: Ask which center has Writing Assistant openings, since the site does not name the select locations.
Plan on at least six months of help, because the group says longer service matters most with young people.
Mentoring can be done virtually or in person.

records.notes: The group's site lists PO Box 11766 as its mailing address, while the IRS record shows 12 E Church Ln; the IRS address is kept as carried, so the owner may want to check it. The five Philadelphia center addresses come from the group's locations page; the Writing Assistant and distribution roles are at select centers that the site does not name. Background check is set to true because the volunteer page says clearances depend on the role; no specific clearance is named, so the Act 153 field is left out. The summary now covers all programs and notes mentors are matched with youth ages 7 to 14. Distribution volunteering was added as food_pantry. Newcomer rating moved from 3 to 2 because the form, clearances and orientation all come before a first shift. The Academy's age range is not stated.

records.name: Mt. Airy Business Improvement District
records.summary: Mt. Airy Business Improvement District is the business district for Germantown Avenue in Mt. Airy. It keeps the commercial strip clean, cares for six small pocket parks, and holds open Zoom meetings where neighbors can hear about and respond to development projects.
records.what_you_do: Cleans the Mt. Airy commercial corridor six days a week and runs projects such as flower baskets, holiday decor, and banners. Offers a facade improvement grant for property and business owners. The board meets on the second Tuesday of the month, and the zoning page lists public zoning and design review meetings for projects along Germantown Avenue.

schedule.text: Board meets on the second Tuesday of the month at 12:15 pm, by Zoom.

access.notes: Zoning meetings can be joined by phone as well as by Zoom.

first_step.how: Register for the next zoning meeting through the Zoom link on the group's zoning page.
first_step.basis: Zoning meetings are online, and residents register through the Zoom links on the page. The page does not mention membership or fees.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each zoning meeting reviews one development project. The listed zoning discussions ran about an hour, and one design review ran 90 minutes. Meetings are held on Zoom with a phone option, and the page does not describe how comments are taken or what the group does with them.
first_visit_tips: Register through the Zoom link on the zoning page, since that is the way in the page lists.
Some meetings can also be joined by phone, so use the dial-in on the meeting listing if you prefer.
Board meetings are on the second Tuesday at 12:15 pm, but the page gives no Zoom link, so email the group for details.

records.notes: Judgment call for the owner: this is a business improvement district, so the rule on businesses with no community program was weighed. It stays publish because it runs public zoning review meetings and maintains pocket parks. A strict reading would make it hide with out_of_scope. Status uses the board's 2026 calendar, which lists an October 5, 2026 annual meeting; the page does not confirm that it was held. The newest zoning meeting listed is October 23, 2025. Annual assessments fall on district property owners, so no cost to neighbors is listed. The summary is corrected because tier 1 called it a neighborhood group, and the group describes itself as a business district.

records.name: Penn Knox Neighborhood Association
records.summary: Penn Knox Neighborhood Association is one of the community organizations registered with the City to review nearby zoning and building proposals in the Upper Northwest part of the city. Neighbors can follow what is planned and speak up.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings are listed for the first Tuesday of the month, 7 to 9 pm, on Zoom.

cost.text: Suggested yearly dues: $10 per person or $25 per household. Any amount is welcome.

first_step.how: Email pennknox.germantown@gmail.com to confirm the next Zoom meeting before you join, since the site's meeting listings stop in 2024.
first_step.basis: The site lists a monthly Zoom meeting, but its newest meeting listing is from 2024, and it does not say outright that neighbors may attend.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings review nearby zoning and building proposals, and the group shares its view with the City and developers. The site lists the first Tuesday of the month from 7 to 9 pm on Zoom. Suggested dues help pay for event permits, legal fees, and newsletter printing, and the site does not describe how a meeting runs.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the next meeting by email before you log on.
Dues are suggested, not required, and the site says a check can be mailed or dropped off.
The site's footer lists a Facebook group and an Instagram account, which may carry newer meeting details.

records.notes: Status changed from active to dormant. The newest activity I could read is minutes listed through March 2024, and the newsletter archive ends in December 2023. The City RCO list used in tier 1 still lists the group, but a registry entry is not treated as activity here. Owner should confirm the group is still meeting before this shows as current. The site's street address and phone fields are unfilled placeholders, so the phone from the City list is kept as carried. The dues page lists a personal email for the treasurer; it was not copied into this record. The street address for quarterly meetings is the Friends Free Library address from the City list, and the site does not confirm the hybrid format on the pages read.

records.name: Pomona Cherokee Civic Council (PCCC) RCO
records.summary: Pomona Cherokee Civic Council (PCCC) RCO is a Registered Community Organization (RCO) in the Upper Northwest part of the city. The City asks developers to talk with RCOs about nearby zoning and building plans, so this is a way for neighbors to have a say.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Germantown Mennonite Church, 21 West Washington Lane, Philadelphia, PA 19144

first_step.how: Email PCCC19144@gmail.com to ask when the next meeting is, then go to Germantown Mennonite Church at 21 West Washington Lane.
first_step.basis: The City lists a meeting place, but no recent meeting notice, schedule or group website was found, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The group has no website of its own: its only listed web page is Facebook, which was not read because it is a lead-only platform. The City's April 13, 2026 Registered Community Organizations list confirms the group, its meeting place at Germantown Mennonite Church, its email, and an expiration year of 2027. That list names Stephanie Vogel as primary contact, while the City layer used in tier 1 names David W. Webber. The tier 1 name is kept, so check which is current. A 2019 Generocity profile, seen only as a search snippet and not opened, describes the council as revived after going inactive. No meeting notice, minutes or news after 2019 was found, so status is unknown rather than active. Search turned up no other website.
